meta.title: Drake Equation / Fermi Paradox
meta.description: The Drake equation as a chain of conditionals: stars form, some have planets, some of those planets are habitable, on some life emerges, some of that life becomes intelligent, some of it communicates, and it stays detectable for a while. Each stage multiplies the previous one by a percentage, with order-of-magnitude (log-uniform) priors after Sandberg, Drexler & Ord's 'Dissolving the Fermi Paradox'. The point of the exercise: with honest uncertainty, the MEDIAN number of communicating civilizations can be modest while the MEAN is enormous — and P(we are alone) is not small.

nodes.title: Star formation rate
nodes.notes: Rate of star formation in the Milky Way. Astronomy pins this reasonably well; the range covers disagreement across surveys.

nodes.title: Percentage of stars with planets
nodes.notes: Post-Kepler this is close to 100%; the lower bound is conservative.

nodes.title: Stars with planets, per year
nodes.notes: Given a star forms, the chance it has planets.

nodes.title: Habitable planets per planetary system
nodes.notes: Planets per planetary system that could support life.

nodes.title: Habitable planets, per year
nodes.notes: Given a star with planets, how many of them could support life.

nodes.title: Percentage of habitable planets where life emerges
nodes.notes: Abiogenesis probability given a habitable planet — genuinely unknown across orders of magnitude. This and f_i dominate the answer.

nodes.title: Planets where life emerges, per year
nodes.notes: Given a habitable planet, the chance life gets started on it.

nodes.title: Percentage of living planets that develop intelligence
nodes.notes: Given life, probability that intelligence evolves.

nodes.title: Planets with intelligent life, per year
nodes.notes: Given life, the chance it becomes intelligent.

nodes.title: Percentage of intelligent species that communicate
nodes.notes: Given intelligence, probability of detectable technology. The unit says what the percentage is of: communicating civilizations per intelligent planet, so the chain ends in civilizations.

nodes.title: Communicating civilizations arising, per year
nodes.notes: Given intelligence, the chance it builds something we could detect.

nodes.title: Civilization lifetime
nodes.notes: How long a communicating civilization remains detectable — from a century to ten billion years.

nodes.title: Communicating civilizations in the galaxy
nodes.notes: Civilizations arising per year times how long each stays detectable: the number out there right now.

nodes.title: P(we are effectively alone)
nodes.notes: Probability that fewer than one other communicating civilization exists — the 'dissolved' Fermi paradox is that this is sizable even when the mean of N is huge.
